title: How to unsubscribe from emails in Gmail on Mac: Manage subscriptions in Safari and Chrome

intro: To unsubscribe from emails in Gmail on Mac, open mail.google.com in Safari or Chrome, click More, then choose Manage subscriptions and click Unsubscribe next to the sender. For a single newsletter, open one of its emails, click Unsubscribe next to the sender's name, then confirm in the pop-up or finish on the sender's website.
tldr: Open mail.google.com in Safari or Chrome, click More, then choose Manage subscriptions.
Click Unsubscribe next to a sender to leave all of that sender's active mailing lists.
For one newsletter, open an email from the sender and click Unsubscribe next to their name.
Block sends future mail to Spam. It does not unsubscribe you from the mailing list.
Changes can take a few days, and Manage subscriptions may still be rolling out to your account.

blocks.text: Before you start with Gmail on your Mac

You need a Mac, Safari or Chrome, and a Gmail account. Google's help pages describe unsubscribing in Gmail on a computer, in a web browser. They do not describe a separate Gmail app for Mac, so this guide uses the Gmail website at mail.google.com.
Sign in before you start. If you open mail.google.com while signed out, Google sends you to its sign-in page. The unsubscribe options need a signed-in session, so you cannot skip that step.
Manage subscriptions: the fastest way to stop a sender

Manage subscriptions is the option to use when one sender fills your inbox. Gmail lists your active subscriptions and sorts them by the sender who emails you most. Each row shows how many emails that sender sent in the past few weeks.

When you click Unsubscribe on a row, Gmail removes you from all active mailing lists tied to that sender. You do not open each newsletter. Google's July 2025 announcement says Gmail also sends the unsubscribe request to the sender for you.
The feature launched on July 8, 2025. Google says it is rolling out gradually on web, Android, and iOS, in select countries. If you do not see it yet, the single email method below still works.
Single email method: stop one newsletter and keep the rest
Use this method when you want to stop one list and keep the sender's other mail. It is also the fallback when Manage subscriptions is missing from your sidebar.

items: Open an email from the sender you want to stop.
Click Unsubscribe next to the sender's name.
In the pop-up, click Unsubscribe. If the only choice is Go to website, click it.
Finish on the sender's site if Gmail sends you there, then return to your inbox.

blocks.text: Be careful with this method. Unsubscribing from one email may remove you from only one mailing list. Gmail may also show a list ID instead of the sender's name, which makes the email harder to recognize.
Unsubscribe, block, or report spam: what each one does
People mix these up all the time. Only one of them is an unsubscribe. The table shows what each choice does, based on Google's help pages.

rows: Yes, all active lists from that sender
A sender that fills your inbox
One newsletter you no longer read
No, future mail goes to Spam
A sender you never want to see in your inbox
No, it flags the mail as spam
blocks.caption: What each option does, based on Google's help pages

blocks.text: Blocking is the mistake people make most often. Google says blocking does not unsubscribe you from the mailing list. It only sends future emails from that sender to Spam, so the sender still has your address.

Report spam is for mail you do not trust. Google's shortcut table lists a spam-report key by its symbol. Reporting spam does not remove you from a list, so pair it with Unsubscribe when you want the mail to stop at the source.
What happens after you click Unsubscribe

Gmail does not always stop mail the moment you click. Google says a sender can take a few days to process the request. You may still get messages in the meantime, so do not judge the result on day one.

The FTC's CAN-SPAM compliance guide sets a firmer deadline. A sender must honor an opt-out request within 10 business days. The guide is dated August 2023, with a January 2024 edit for inflation-adjusted penalties.
If mail keeps arriving after that window, the sender is not following the rule. Report it as spam using the spam-report key, and note the sender's name so you can check again later.
Why some senders make unsubscribing harder

Big senders follow stricter rules. Since February 1, 2024, senders that send more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail must support one-click unsubscribe. They need the List-Unsubscribe-Post header with the One-Click value, plus a List-Unsubscribe header.

Smaller senders are not bound by that rule. Their emails may only offer Go to website, and you must finish the process on their site. That can take a few more clicks, and the steps depend on the sender's site.
Keyboard shortcuts for Gmail on Mac
Gmail keyboard shortcuts are off until you turn them on. Open Settings with the gear icon, choose See all settings, then find Keyboard shortcuts, select On, and click Save Changes.

Google's shortcut table has no unsubscribe key. The key it lists for reporting spam is shown as a symbol, so check which symbol your own keyboard prints on that key, because the key position changes with the layout.
Google's shortcut page says PCs use Ctrl where this guide says ⌘, so ⌘ is the Mac key to remember. Shortcuts speed up the work, but clicking through Manage subscriptions does the same job.
Common mistakes people make
The first mistake is clicking Block when you meant Unsubscribe. The mail stops landing in your inbox, so the inbox looks clean. The sender still keeps your address on its list.

The second mistake is stopping at one email. A sender can run several mailing lists. Open More, then Manage subscriptions, to see every list tied to that sender, and unsubscribe from each one you do not want.
The third mistake is expecting instant results. A few days is normal, according to Google. Give it time before you assume the sender ignored you.

The fourth mistake is checking the wrong account. If you use more than one Google account, make sure you are signed in to the one that receives the mail. The subscriptions you see belong to the account you are signed in to.
When Manage subscriptions does not show up

The feature is still rolling out, so it may not appear on your account yet. Google says so on its Manage subscriptions help page. Mailmop's guide, dated September 2, 2026, starts its fix list with updating the Gmail app and reopening it.

Mailmop also says personal accounts got the feature first and work or school accounts later. It suggests using Gmail itself rather than a mail app, turning off Basic HTML view, and checking the Gmail language setting. Try each fix before you give up on the feature.
Until it appears, use the single email method. Click Unsubscribe in each message, and use Go to website when Gmail offers it.
If you read Gmail in Apple Mail

Google's setup page lists Apple Mail as a client you can connect to Gmail. Mailmop advises using Gmail itself for subscription changes. So open mail.google.com in Safari or Chrome when you want Manage subscriptions, even if you read mail elsewhere.
Keep the senders you still want

Not every sender should go. Some newsletters are worth reading later. For those, a filter can send mail to a label or skip your inbox without changing your subscription. Read [how to create a filter in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail) for the browser steps.
Work through the list one sender at a time. Unsubscribe from the ones you no longer read, and keep the rest. You can repeat the steps next month when new senders appear.
A short checklist before you close the tab

items: Open More, then Manage subscriptions, and read through the top senders.
Unsubscribe from anything you no longer read. Use Go to website when that is the only option.
Check the Spam folder for a sender you blocked by mistake, and click Report not spam.
Wait several days, then check whether the mail has stopped.

faq.question: Is there a Gmail app for Mac that lets me unsubscribe?
faq.answer: Google's unsubscribe help pages describe the Gmail website in a browser. They do not describe a separate Mac app, so open mail.google.com in Safari or Chrome. The steps in this guide are the browser steps.

faq.question: Does unsubscribing from one email stop every email from that sender?
faq.answer: Not always. Unsubscribing from one email may remove you from only one mailing list. Open More, then Manage subscriptions, to see every list tied to that sender.

faq.question: How long does it take for unsubscribed emails to stop?
faq.answer: Google says it can take a few days, and you may still get messages in the meantime. The FTC gives senders 10 business days to honor an opt-out request. If mail continues past that window, report it as spam.

faq.question: What is the difference between unsubscribing and blocking in Gmail?
faq.answer: Unsubscribing removes you from the sender's active mailing lists. Blocking only sends future emails from that sender to Spam. Google says blocking does not unsubscribe you, so choose Unsubscribe when you want the mail to stop at the source.

faq.question: Why don't I see Manage subscriptions in my Gmail on Mac?
faq.answer: Google says the feature is gradually rolling out, so it may not be available on your account yet. Mailmop says personal accounts got it first and work or school accounts later. Try the Gmail website, update your Gmail app, and check your language setting.

faq.question: Does the one-click unsubscribe rule apply to every sender?
faq.answer: No. Since February 1, 2024, the rule covers senders that send more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail. Smaller senders are not bound by it, so you may only see a Go to website option.

faq.question: Does Report spam unsubscribe me from a list?
faq.answer: No. Google's keyboard shortcut table lists a spam-report key and has no unsubscribe key. Reporting spam flags the message. Use Unsubscribe in Manage subscriptions to leave the list.

task: Unsubscribe from emails in Gmail on a Mac
appliesTo: Gmail at mail.google.com in Safari or Chrome on macOS
requirements: A Mac with Safari or Chrome installed
A Gmail account you can sign in to at mail.google.com
A few minutes to scroll through your subscriptions
Keyboard shortcuts turned on, only if you want the spam-report key

steps.name: Open Gmail in your browser
steps.text: In Safari or Chrome, go to mail.google.com and sign in to the Google account whose mail you want to clean up. If you see a sign-in page, you are signed out, so sign in first.

steps.name: Show the left column
steps.text: Look at the left side of the Gmail window. If the column is hidden, click the menu icon in the top-left corner, the one with horizontal lines. Google's help says to click More on the left.
steps.tip: The sidebar can be collapsed or open, and the exact spot can shift with it.

steps.name: Click More
steps.text: Click More in the left column. The list expands and shows more options, including Manage subscriptions.

steps.name: Open Manage subscriptions
steps.text: Click Manage subscriptions. Gmail lists your active subscriptions, sorted by the sender who emails you most often. Each row shows how many emails that sender sent in the past few weeks.

steps.name: Click Unsubscribe on a sender's row
steps.text: Find the sender you want to stop, then click Unsubscribe next to their recent email count. Gmail removes you from all active mailing lists tied to that sender.
steps.tip: This covers the whole sender. If you only want one newsletter, use the single email method instead.

steps.name: Finish in the pop-up
steps.text: If the pop-up offers Go to website, click it and finish on the sender's site. If it offers Unsubscribe, click it. Block is a different choice, and it does not unsubscribe you.
steps.tip: If a new email from this sender lands in Spam with a banner, click Report not spam to bring it back.

steps.name: Wait a few days
steps.text: Google says the sender can take a few days to process the request. Expect some mail in the meantime, and check again before you decide the unsubscribe failed.

shortcuts.action: Report the sender's mail as spam (not an unsubscribe)

troubleshooting.problem: I don't see Manage subscriptions under More
troubleshooting.fix: The feature is still rolling out. Update the Gmail app if you use one, and use Gmail in the browser instead of a mail app. Turn off Basic HTML view and check the Gmail language setting. Work or school accounts may get it later.

troubleshooting.problem: The pop-up only shows Go to website
troubleshooting.fix: Click Go to website. Google says some senders show only that option, and you must finish on their site. Look for a preferences page or an unsubscribe link, and expect a few more clicks.

troubleshooting.problem: Emails keep coming after I clicked Unsubscribe
troubleshooting.fix: Google says the sender can take a few days to process the request. The FTC gives senders 10 business days to honor an opt-out. If mail continues past that, report it as spam using the spam-report key.

troubleshooting.problem: A sender's new mail goes straight to Spam
troubleshooting.fix: Gmail can move new mail from a sender to Spam with a banner. Click Report not spam to move that mail back to your inbox.

troubleshooting.problem: The sender appears as a list ID, not a name
troubleshooting.fix: Gmail may show a list ID instead of the sender's name. To find all of a sender's subscriptions, open More, then Manage subscriptions.
